results.previous_best: \(\frac{1}{2}\)-approximation in linear time for arbitrary inputs; \((\frac{1}{2}+\delta)\)-approximation in \(O(n^{1+\varepsilon})\) for equal-length inputs only [RS20]
results.quote: For all \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists an absolute constant \(\delta=\delta(\varepsilon)>0\) and a deterministic algorithm that, given two binary strings _x_ and _y_ of not-necessarily-equal length, outputs a \((\frac{1}{2}+\delta)\)-approximation of the longest common subsequence in time \(O(n^{1+\varepsilon})\) where _n_=max(|_x_|,|_y_|).

results.previous_best: \(\frac{1}{q}\)-approximation in linear time for arbitrary inputs; \((\frac{1}{q}+\delta)\)-approximation in \(O(n^{1+\varepsilon})\) for equal-length inputs only [AW21]
results.quote: For all \(\varepsilon>0\) and integers \(q\ge 2\), there exists an absolute constant \(\delta=\delta(\varepsilon)>0\) and a deterministic algorithm that, given two q-ary strings _x_ and _y_ of not-necessarily-equal length, outputs a \((\frac{1}{q}+\delta)\)-approximation of the longest common subsequence in time \(O(n^{1+\varepsilon})\) where _n_=max(|_x_|,|_y_|).
